verdict: Oracle's revenue rose 9% to $14.1B as its cloud business kept accelerating — cloud services brought in $10.8B — and it kept $3.15B as profit, though $866M of interest on its debt pile took a real bite.

segments.name: Cloud services & license support
segments.note: Renting Oracle's cloud, plus support for the software customers already run — the steady base of the business, 77% of all revenue.

segments.name: Cloud license & on-premise license
segments.note: New software licenses sold outright, for customers running Oracle on their own machines — shrinking as customers move to cloud subscriptions instead.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Consulting and support services that help customers run Oracle products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the cloud platform and the database software — up 11% YoY as Oracle races to add AI capacity.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office, up 3% YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge, down 22% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Restructuring charges of $84M plus $31M of acquisition-related costs.

otherDetail: Interest expense of $866M on Oracle's debt pile, partly offset by $36M of other non-operating income, net.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: The backlog jumped 49%
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — work customers have signed for but not yet paid for — reached $97B, up 49% from a year ago. Cloud customers, including AI companies renting Oracle's data centers, are booking capacity well ahead.

takeaways.title: Cloud is carrying the growth
takeaways.text: Cloud services and license support revenue rose 12% to $10.8B — over three-quarters of all revenue — while old-style licenses barely grew and hardware and services shrank. The mix keeps shifting toward recurring cloud rent.

takeaways.title: Debt is the quiet cost
takeaways.text: Oracle paid $866M of interest in a single quarter on debt taken on to build data centers and buy back stock. Profit still rose 26%, but interest now eats about a fifth of operating income.

footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud services and license support', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue. Segment names follow Oracle's fiscal 2025 presentation; from fiscal 2026 Oracle regrouped its reporting into Cloud, Software, Hardware and Services.
